task: Independent source-only adjudication of Charismatic Decree Recruit with one warrior in supply

conclusion.answer: These inputs establish failure to fully perform the two-warrior Recruit and consequent immediate Turmoil. They do not expressly sequence the maximum-possible placement in 1.5.4 against the immediate-Turmoil trigger in 7.5.2. I cannot certify either one placed or one retained as uniquely compelled without an interpretation of that timing.
certain_effects: A full Charismatic Recruit requires two warriors, not one.
Only one warrior is available from the default placement source.
The Decree action cannot be fully performed.
Turmoil follows; placing one cannot satisfy the full Decree action and avert Turmoil.
Turmoil resolves Humiliate, Purge, Depose (with A New Clutch if applicable), then Rest; Daylight ends and Evening begins.
conclusion.not_claimed: This is not a claim that an external official ruling does not exist; none was consulted or authorized.

source_quotes.quote_normalized_linewraps_and_discretio: Precedence. If a card conflicts with the Law, follow the card. If the Learning to Play guide conflicts with the Law, follow the Law. If you can follow both a general rule and a faction or hireling rule, follow both; if you cannot, follow the faction or hireling rule.
Use of Cannot. The term cannot is absolute. It cannot be overridden unless explicitly instructed.
Unclear Resolutions and Choices. Whenever it is unclear what order simultaneous effects should resolve in, or which player should make a decision, the player taking their turn chooses.

Interrupts. You cannot interrupt an action (including a compound action such as the Marquise’s March), ability (such as the Corvids’ Exposure), or persistent effect (such as the Eyrie Emigre card) with another effect unless it explicitly allows it. (For example, the Armorers card says it is used “In battle...”).
Limits. Pieces are limited by the contents of the game. Do not use proxy pieces if you run out.

Piece Manipulation. Pieces are placed and removed as defined in the Glossary (G.20, G.24). If you are prompted to place, take, or remove pieces but you cannot do so fully, you must place, take, or remove the maximum number possible. (This does not let you avoid costs or prerequisites. You just cannot do less than the most you can.)

Resolve the Decree. You must resolve the Decree, starting with the leftmost column and moving right. In each column, you must resolve all of its cards, but in any order. For each card, you must take the action listed for its column, as follows. If you cannot fully take an action, you immediately fall into turmoil (7.7).
Recruit. Place a warrior in any clearing with a roost whose suit matches the card suit.
If you cannot fully take an action in the Decree (7.5.2) for any reason, you fall into turmoil. You must take the Turmoil action as follows in order.
Step 1: Humiliate. Lose one victory point per bird card (including Loyal Viziers) on the Decree.
Step 2: Purge. Discard all of the cards on the Decree except your Loyal Viziers.

Step 3: Depose. Flip your current leader face down and set it aside, choose a new leader from those face up, and place on your faction board. Tuck your Loyal Viziers into the Decree spaces listed on your new leader.
A New Clutch. If you must choose a new leader but none are face up, flip them all face up.
Step 4: Rest. End Daylight and begin Evening.
Charismatic. Loyal Viziers begin on Recruit and Battle. Whenever you take a Recruit action, you must place two warriors instead of one.

Place. Take the prompted piece from the prompted source and put it in the prompted destination. Usually, no source is specified—in this case, take it from its supply, or take the leftmost prompted piece if it is on a track. Put is shorthand for Place.

reasoning.point: 7.8.2 changes the quantity to two; 7.5.2.I supplies the matching-roost destination. G.20 supplies the default supply source. 1.5.1 disallows proxy completion.

1.5.4 is an imperative to place the maximum possible when a placement prompt cannot be fully fulfilled. Its exception concerns costs or prerequisites. The scenario stipulates a legal destination and supplies no separate payment. Neither 7.5.2.I nor 7.8.2 explicitly phrases possession of two supply warriors as a prerequisite for beginning the action.

7.5.2, specifically its final sentence, supplies the word immediately and is the authoritative timing passage. 7.7 repeats the inability-to-fully-take condition and supplies the subsequent Turmoil procedure; 7.8.2 supplies quantity, not timing.

A compatible reading is that the required Recruit constitutes the placement prompt, so 1.5.4 requires the one possible placement, while the unchanged two-warrior requirement means the Decree action is still incomplete and immediately causes Turmoil. Here immediately forbids continuing the Decree after its failed action; it does not retroactively cancel the physical placement that its prompt required. This preserves both rules if their trigger is resolved this way.

An alternative reading applies the inability condition at the outset of the required action. Since full two-warrior placement is already impossible, 7.5.2 directs immediate Turmoil before a placement can occur. If immediate is read as preempting the partial-placement instruction, there is a timing incompatibility with 1.5.4, and 1.1.1 gives the Eyrie faction rule priority. The warrior stays in supply on this reading.

1.1.1 first requires following both rules when possible; it does not automatically discard 1.5.4 merely because Charismatic or the Decree is faction-specific. Quantity alone is not an actual incompatibility: 1.5.4 expressly addresses instructions that cannot be fulfilled completely. The potential incompatibility is the sequencing implied by immediately, not whether the full requirement is two.

The source does not explicitly say to check full-action feasibility before beginning the placement prompt, nor explicitly say to execute the maximum partial placement before evaluating Decree failure. Selecting either order supplies an interpretation. Invoking faction precedence alone presumes the preemption that must first be established; invoking maximum placement alone leaves the immediate language unexamined.

1.4.2 does not itself settle when the incomplete-action trigger is evaluated. It bars interruption unless explicitly allowed; the specific immediate-Turmoil instruction can be read as allowing an interruption, but does not expressly state whether a placement has already occurred. 1.1.3 concerns simultaneous effects; the text does not explicitly classify these two instructions as simultaneous effects, so I do not infer a free player choice between placement outcomes.

Under either timing reading, execute the four ordered Turmoil steps. No cited Turmoil step returns a warrior to supply or retroactively undoes a completed placement. Thus the candidate place-one reading leaves that warrior in the legal roost clearing, while the candidate preemption reading leaves it in supply.

alternatives_considered.assessment: Textually supported by the mandatory maximum-possible placement and a compatible reading of failure timing; not expressly sequenced in the source.

alternatives_considered.outcome: Place none; immediate Turmoil; one remains in supply
alternatives_considered.assessment: Textually supported by an outset/preemption reading of immediately and faction priority if an actual timing conflict exists; not expressly stated as a before-placement feasibility check.
Rejected: does not fully meet the Charismatic two-warrior requirement and ignores 7.5.2/7.7.

alternatives_considered.outcome: Player freely chooses whether to place one
alternatives_considered.assessment: Not established: 1.1.3 does not expressly classify the competing instructions as simultaneous; underdetermination of interpretation is not a game permission.

alternatives_considered.outcome: Place one and then return it to supply during Turmoil
alternatives_considered.assessment: Rejected as unsupported: no cited Turmoil step instructs reversal.

certainty.underdetermination_assessment: moderate; reasonable readers may consider ordinary immediate language sufficient for the preemption reading, or regard the mandatory maximum-placement rule as already reconciling both. The artifact distinguishes these interpretations rather than presenting either as an explicit worked ruling.
